device.name: Keithley 2200 series programmable DC power supply (KEI2220S)

facts.text: The upstream KEI2220S class defines a misspelled __innit__ routine containing the VISA resource open
The README says the program uses National Instruments VISA to communicate with the Keithley Series 2200 Programmable DC Power Supplies
The README says the author could not test the code on the instrument
The __innit__ parameter is inst_address, but open_resource is called with self.instr_address, which the routine never sets
get_info queries *IDN? and splits the reply into manufacturer, model, serial number and firmware version
A new current measurement is initiated with MEAS:CURR? and a new voltage measurement with MEAS:VOLT?
FETCh:POW? returns the last measured output power without initiating a measurement; the instrument recomputes power about every 100 ms
set_curr writes CURR and accepts a per-model maximum of 1.2, 1.5, 2.5, 3 or 5 A
set_volt writes VOLT and its code accepts only 0 through 30 V
set_ovp writes VOLT:PROT and its code accepts only 0 through 30 V
set_output_state contains OUTP writes and get_output_state queries OUTP?; its ON/OFF string branch appends literal .upper() text
set_ovp_state contains VOLT:PROT:STAT writes and queries; its ON/OFF string branch appends literal .upper() text

operator_required.name: voltage
operator_required.reason: the clone's set_volt writes VOLT but its code check is only 0 through 30 V (2220 Programmable DC Power Supplies.py:695-699), while set_curr lists a 2200-60-2 and a 2200-72-1 model (2220 Programmable DC Power Supplies.py:245-257); the voltage range of the installed unit is an operator decision

operator_required.name: current
operator_required.reason: the clone's set_curr writes CURR and lists different per-model maxima of 1.2, 1.5, 2.5, 3 and 5 A (2220 Programmable DC Power Supplies.py:245-257) but never states which model is connected; the current limit of the installed unit is an operator decision

operator_required.name: overvoltage_protection
operator_required.reason: the clone's set_ovp writes VOLT:PROT but its code check is only 0 through 30 V (2220 Programmable DC Power Supplies.py:721-725), which does not cover the 60 V and 72 V models the class handles; the protection range of the installed unit is an operator decision

safe_state.description: output disabled with OUTP OFF (voltage and current set points left unchanged)
